subject: Pegasus: cryptographic controls and BYO key evidence request
messages:

Subject: Pegasus - cryptography controls request (KMS/BYOK/HSM)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our vendor review we need a detailed response to a short set of technical questions focused on key management and cryptographic controls before we proceed to legal procurement. Specifically:

- Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with an HSM-backed import flow?
- Can customers hold keys in their cloud KMS (Azure/GC/KeyVault) and have Redwood reference them for hosted inference?
- What is the rotation policy and how do you surface rotation audit evidence?
- TLS configuration and cipher suites for data-in-transit: do you support minimum TLS1.2 with specific ciphers?
- Evidence: can you provide short artifacts (diagrams, config excerpts, logs) that demonstrate key import, key-use segregation, and key rotation events?

We appreciate a concise, evidence-backed reply. If helpful we can set a 30-minute call to walk through any items.

Best,
Emma Clarkson
Procurement Manager
Pegasus AI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@pegasusai.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, security@pegasusai.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus - cryptography controls request (KMS/BYOK/HSM)

Emma,

Thanks for the clear list — appreciate the context. Short answers up front, followed by a couple of artifacts attached and a pointer to where you can download full evidence.

1) BYOK + HSM import: Yes. We support BYOK via an HSM-backed import flow. Customers provide a key-wrapping public key; Redwood generates a key-encrypting key (KEK) which is imported into the HSM-backed provider during onboarding. We support both PKCS#8 wrapped key imports and cloud-provider key references.

2) Cloud KMS referencing: Yes. For hosted inference we support references to customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. We use the cloud provider's envelope encryption APIs so the plaintext key material never traverses Redwood control plane.

3) Rotation policy & evidence: Rotation can be automated (recommended cadence is 90 days) or customer-triggered. Rotation is implemented as a new key version with a graceful KV cache and traffic draining period; old versions remain for decryption of persisted artifacts for a configurable retention window. Audit records for key-rotate operations are logged to our immutable audit store and exported to customer-specified SIEM/Cloud Audit (we attached a rotation event sample).

4) TLS & ciphers: We enforce TLS1.2+ across all external endpoints; default policy requires TLS1.3 where supported and negotiates strong cipher suites (AES-GCM and CHACHA20_POLY1305). We publish our TLS profile in the attached diagram and can provide per-region cipher lists on request.

5) Evidence: Attached: redwood_kms_byo_summary.pdf (process and controls), hsm_integration_diagram.png (logical flow), rotation_policy_snapshot.txt (sample audit lines). Full packet available via the Drive link below.

If you prefer a short technical call, Naomi (copied) is our Security Engineering lead and can join. Would Friday 3/14 10am PT work for you?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus - cryptography controls request (KMS/BYOK/HSM)

Emma / Pegasus security team,

Quick technical additions from security: a couple of details you asked for that are easiest to show here.

- HSMs: we integrate with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSM clusters for key wrapping and split-key operations in our Dedicated and Private modes; for Hosted we rely on cloud-provider HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Google Cloud HSM).
- Key usage separation: key material used for runtime inference is held in isolated envelopes; signing and audit keys are separate key types with restricted IAM roles.
- Import flow: import includes an import-token exchange, signature proof from the customer, and an HSM-wrapped import operation so Redwood never sees unwrapped private key bits.
- Rotation evidence snippet: included below as a sample event log line (redacted):

On 2026-03-10T22:12:07Z audit:event=key_rotate key_id=proj-pegasus/enc-001 performed_by=automation user=system request_id=req-9f2c

Attached is a small text file with a few redacted audit lines and the high-level integration diagram. We can also produce a timeboxed redaction for any PII if required.

Naomi Feldman
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
